page.layout: One page of text, full width: a Latin verse stanza at the top, then a row of ornaments, then a Dutch verse poem, then an italic closing line. At the foot, the signature "C 3" on the left and the catchword "Unde" on the right.

main_text.p: Tu mentem geniumq; tuum majoribus aufis Erigis, & viridi vestitum tempora daphne Te cupis Aoniis quondam inclarescere chartis En Christus, non Papa-Goel, non Papa sed Abba Ter sonteis salvans diram compescit Erynnin: Et Christi meritum & rubentem sanguinis un-dam Miramur, sacris fideiq; amplectimur ulnis.

GElyck de roode Zee geheel gedaen verdrincken Het Phaaronsche Heyr, t'vvelck moedig dede blin-cken Alldus de roode Zee den grooten Ocean K'segge Christus Bloed Versoening vvercken kan Wel Wel Christ Mensche-God sall richten myne Sacken Ende vaster mynen Soen by synen Vader macken Als Jonathan vvel eer vor David heft gedaan Doe tegens hem de Saul met vvrake ging belaën; Vast sondig is myn Sond, edoch heb ick vernomen Van mynen soeten Franck, dat Christus is gekomen Zuyt scheldend my daer van, ten Vader gaet hy in Als mynen Advocat, en mynen Benjamin.
Sic utroq; Idiomate gratulabundus ascinit D. G.

page.notes: The row of ornaments between the two poems is decoration and is not transcribed. No page number is printed; only the signature C 3 and the catchword Unde. The Dutch stanza is set with the spelling vv for w and with black-letter-free roman type throughout; the forms are copied as printed.
